the world's largest manufacturers of aerostructures for commercial aircraft, defence platforms, and business/regional jets. Built on more than 100 years of aviation experience, Spirit is headquartered in Wichita, US, with ~14,800 employees globally. It has facilities in the US, UK (Belfast (Short Brother PLC) and Prestwick), France, Malaysia and Morocco. With expertise in aluminum and advanced composite manufacturing solutions, Spirit’s core products include integrated wings and wing components, fuselages, pylons and engine nacelles. It also has a growing aftermarket and space business. Spirit UK is one of the largest aerospace companies in the UK, with a total of ~ 3600 employees across its sites in Northern Ireland (c2,700) and Prestwick (c900). It is a major driver in the local economies where its sites are based. Spirit UK has over 700 approved UK suppliers, and is a key mentor in the aerospace industry’s SC21 supply chain development programme, working with suppliers to improve their competitiveness and win more high-value global work packages. Spirit UK is a research-intensive company, and its two UK sites are centres of excellence for the design, manufacture and after-market support of complex aerostructures in metal and advanced composites, including wings, nacelles, fuselages and spoilers. The principal activities of Spirit’s Belfast operations are t

after-market support of complex aerostructures in metal and advanced composites, including wings, nacelles, fuselages and spoilers. The principal activities of Spirit’s Belfast operations are the design, development, manufacture and assembly of major aircraft structural components (including wings, fuselages, engine nacelles and flight components) and provision of aftermarket component repair and overhaul, as well as other engineering services. Many of the programmes in which the company is involved has required significant R&D investment, including in the A220 advanced composite wing programme. At over �520m, this was the largest ever single inward investment in Northern Ireland, which will sustain over 1000 high-value jobs at peak production and many more in the UK supply chain. Spirit Prestwick’s main activities are the design, development, manufacture and assembly of airframes, which consist principally of wing structure components. New product development includes design, development and materials research. The site has also formally opened its new Aerospace Innovation Centre – a �25m investment – where it will be collaborating with industrial, academic and supply chain partners on developing the new technologies and skills required for future sustainable aircraft platforms. mpliTex range is also the most unique one: The powerRibs technology is based on the concept of the leafveins, rigidifying a surface with minimum weight.
